simple.meaning: חָמַם (châmam) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be hot (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Exodus, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, Job, Psalms, and 3 more, beginning at Exodus 16:21. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָמַם (H2552).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: They gathered it morning by morning, everyone according to his eating. When the sun grew hot, it melted.

Therefore his servants said to him, “Let a young virgin be sought for my lord the king. Let her stand before the king, and cherish him; and let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may keep warm.”
He went up, and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself on him; and the child’s flesh grew warm.
